newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts up with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts up with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a quiet session, with front months scoring modest gains on reports of firmer cash, then reacting very little on ACCESS after weekly AGA stock data.

April firmed 3.6 cents to close at $1.955 per million British thermal units, then in after-hours ACCESS trade inched to $1.96-7 on the AGA data. May settled 2.5 cents higher at $2.028. Others were mixed, with some 1998s down slightly.
"It (the AGA number) doesn't mean much anymore. Winter is almost over, but the net injection in the producing region explains some of the recent strength in the cash," said one.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 57 bcf, in line with expectations, but climbed to 191 bcf, or 26 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage, which fell by 49 bcf, rose to 225 bcf, or 75 percent, over last year. Producing region inventories gained three bcf.

With cooler Northeast weather ahead and some heat expected in the South, some agreed the seasonal bottom may be in place. But most saw little reason for prices to move far in either direction near-term.

Technical traders still pegged key resistance in April at $2.04, with a close above that number likely to lead to a test of the mid-teens. Further selling was seen at $2.28. Minor support was at $1.88, with better buying expected at $1.78-1.80 and then at the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained several cents Wednesday to the low-$1.90s, about 20 cents over March indices. Midcon pipes firmed a nickel to the mid-$1.80s, more than 20 cents above March 1 levels. New York city gate swing gas was a few cents higher in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
The 12-month strip gained 1.8 cents to $2.133. NYMEX said an estimated 31,426 contracts traded, down slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 32,044.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, April finished three cents higher at $1.72, while deferreds ended up by one-half to 2.1 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.6 cent to 23.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 203 lots changed hands, up from Tuesday's total of 189.
